segments.translation_text: The opposite of meditation that should be discarded is distraction. The antidote is realization of the selflessness of phenomena, through which one possesses primordial wisdom of non-conceptualization of the three cycles. The outcome that is a temporary result is becoming able to completely fulfill the wishes of other sentient beings. The ultimate result is placing sentient beings in the nirvana of one of the three vehicles according to their motivation. Thus, beings are completely matured through the four dharmas.

The antidote is realization of the selflessness of phenomena, through which one possesses primordial wisdom of non-conceptualization of the three cycles. The outcome that is a temporary result is becoming able to completely fulfill the wishes of other sentient beings. The ultimate result is placing sentient beings in the nirvana of one of the three vehicles according to their motivation. Thus, beings are completely matured through the four dharmas.[p.264][[A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas]]

segments.translation_text: Meaningful nature is to focus the mind single-pointedly on the object of analysis. The meaningful cause is not forgetting the object of meditation, based on mindfulness and diligence. The meaningful result is the arising of happiness that is freedom from harm. Meaningful action is attaining sovereign control of the six types of clairvoyance, three types of liberation, four types of samadhi, and four limitless meditations. Meaningful possession means that the good qualities are possessed as described, such as "meditation is chief among all Dharmas.”

segments.translation_text: Calm abiding, or shamatha, meditation is known by that term because when placed upon an object, the mind abides in perfect stability and singlepointedness. Insight meditation, or vipassana, is the ability to correctly discriminate all phenomena.

Insight meditation,51In the Tibetan language, vipassana is "lagtong.” In Sanskrit it is "vipassana.” or vipassana, is the ability to correctly discriminate all phenomena.

segments.translation_text: Worldly meditative experience is considered inferior because it is characterized by less pleasure and more clinging toward the aggregates which disintegrate. It may also be completely debased and deluded by the defilements. Therefore it is considered inferior.

segments.translation_text: Arhats’ and Prateka Buddhas’ meditative experience is characterized by the individual experience of pleasure and clinging to the extreme of peace. segments.translation_text: One may wonder, "How can I overcome distractions?” The body dwells in isolation by abandoning association with many beings. The mind also dwells in isolation by abandoning conceptual thoughts such as inclination toward desire, etc. Through this, external and internal distractions will not occur. In order to abandon defilements, distractions must be abandoned, which depends upon isolation. Therefore, the Lord said:

segments.translation_text: Association with ordinary childlike beings and indulgence in non-virtuous sinful actions similar to theirs will certainly cause falling into lower rebirth. Not associating with them and practicing according to the Dharma of the Noble Ones will cause them to dislike and hate me. By acting like them, I myself will fall into lower rebirth, and by acting unlike them they will be angry at me, so therefore what is the use of ever relying on these childlike beings? There is no benefit.

segments.translation_html:
Jealous toward superiors, competitive toward equals, 
Arrogant toward inferiors, conceited when praised,
Anger arises when unpleasant words are said.
When could benefit be gained from the childish?

segments.wylie: gzhan yang byis pa rnams ni rang bas yon tan mtho ba rnams la phrag dog gi sgo nas mi bzod pa dang mnyam pa rnams la 'gran sems kyi sgo nas rtsod pa dang*/_dma' ba rnams la nga rgyal gyi sgo nas brnyas pa dang*/_yon tan brjod cing bstod na dregs par 'gyur ba dang*/_skyon nas smras shing mi snyan pa brjod na khong khro skye bar 'gyur ba'i phyir/_dus nam zhig gang zag byis pa bsten pa las phan par 'gyur ba ci zhig thob ste mi thob pa nyid do/_/
segments.translation_text: Also, due to jealousy, the childlike cannot tolerate those whose good qualities are superior to theirs. With thoughts of competition, they argue with those who are equal to them. With thoughts of pride and conceit, they have contempt toward those who are lower than themselves. If they are praised by describing their good qualities, they become arrogant. If they are criticized by describing their faults, they become angry. What benefit can ever be found by relying on the childlike? There is no benefit.

segments.translation_text: If there are some who dislike and therefore blame, and others who praise, what is the use of feeling joy in the praise of a few? There is no use. If there are others who are pleased and therefore praise, and others who blame, what is the use of feeling dislike at some blame? There is no use. Therefore, the eight worldly concerns are without essence or benefit.

segments.translation_html:

segments.translation_text: Sentient beings have many different accumulated karmas and different motivations and interests. Even the Buddhas who possess ultimately skillful methods cannot please everyone. Then, how can a simple person like me expect to please all beings? Therefore, for the time being, I should give up thoughts of making them happy and rely on seclusion.

segments.translation_html: In delusion, one may think, "This body is a unit.” In the beginning, the body’s flesh, bones, and so forth emerged simultaneously at birth, but at the end of life, when death comes, each of these will completely disintegrate. If this happens to the body, then what need to mention the inevitable separation from friends and relatives? Think thus and practice mindfulness of disintegration.

segments.translation_html:
At birth, one is born alone;

segments.translation_text: In the beginning, at birth, one is born alone. In the end, at death, one will die alone. Thus practice mindfulness of the consequences of attachment to friends.

segments.translation_html:

segments.translation_html:
Therefore, with great joy
Pleasure, and less hardship in a shady grove,
Completely pacify all distractions.
Thus dwell alone with oneself.

segments.translation_text: Dwelling in isolation has many positive qualities. The forest is an extremely attractive and pleasant place where there is no need to worry about family members such as spouses, so there is less hardship. The happiness of higher birth and certain liberation will arise and all distractions of body, voice, and mind will be pacified. Aspire to dwell always in isolated places. The Moonlight Sutra states:

segments.translation_text: Thus, isolate the body by abandoning busy worldly projects. In order to also isolate the mind, give up and abandon all types of defiled and unspecified conceptual thoughts. Single-pointedly think only of enlightenment thought. Meditate calm abiding in order to equalize samadhi, and meditate insight meditation in order to tame the mind through wisdom. Thus be diligent in meditating the profound path of integration.

segments.translation_text: Excessive attachments and indulgence in the five desire objects have a multitude of faults and disadvantages in this life and the next. For instance, lusting after others’ women causes severe suffering in this life, such as being killed, tied up, and stabbed. In the next life, it brings the endless suffering of falling into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, and the like. Therefore abandon conceptual thoughts that generate desire.

segments.translation_text: Carefully analyze the object of desire with whom one wishes to experience the excellent joy of embrace. That which is embraced is nothing but a skeleton of 360 joints. Permanent sovereign control and possession is lacking. Why not enter the state beyond sorrow, which is uncontaminated bliss, rather than being attached to, and later strongly clinging to a contaminated state? The state beyond sorrow is what should be pursued; therefore abandon reliance on lust.

segments.translation_text: Whether or not you see her face, it will eventually be sent to the cemetery. Why run in fear from the very face that was the object of attachment, which one eagerly desired to look upon with a defiled mind, after it is sent to the cemetery and its appearance revealed with veil removed, and the face is damaged by vultures? It is unsuitable to run away. If you wish to run, then why eagerly and lustfully wish to behold it before it is sent to the cemetery?

segments.translation_text: When alive, you guarded and protected her from even being seen by others. Then why not guard and protect your object of attachment from being sent to the cemetery for animals and vultures? If you feel stinginess and clinging about her face, why not guard it from being eaten by vultures and the like? If you don’t guard it then, why guard it so stingily before that?

segments.translation_text: Analyzing carefully, the heap of flesh in the cemetery is food for animals, such as vultures and jackals. Why decorate their food with flower garlands, anointing it with scented water, and adorning it with jewelry such as rings? To see it as attractive and to decorate and venerate it is extremely deluded.

segments.translation_text: If lust arises toward an object of attachment, such as a female body, when it is covered by clothing and skin, then if that object of attachment is not covered by clothing and skin and is left in the cemetery, why don’t you still like it? Lust should arise toward that, too. However, if you think that is an impure skeleton, and useless, then why embrace that same thing when it is covered by skin and the like? They are equal because it is inappropriate to be attached to either, and they are both impure.

segments.translation_html:
Not enjoying a pillow
Made of soft cotton smooth to the touch,
Foolish ones lust for
The impure and odorous.

segments.translation_text: If you think that you desire it because of the pleasant smell, in that case, why don’t you lust after and enjoy an attractive and enticing pillow, which is filled with soft cotton? The pillow produces no odor or impure substances. Whereas the bodies to which lustful ones are attached are filled with impurity, but in delusion, they are regarded as pure. Delightedly lusting after them is extremely inappropriate.

Others’ bodies are pouches filled with impurity. Lusting after and being attached to impurity is completely inappropriate.

segments.translation_html:
If you say that you prefer flesh with a mind,
Then what you desire cannot be touched or seen;
That which can is not the mind.
What is the use of such a meaningless embrace?

segments.wylie: de ni mi 'dod de sems yod pa la reg cing blta'o snyam na khyod 'dod pa'i sems gang yin pa de ni [p.-257] [[rab gsal snang ba]] gzugs can ma yin pas reg pa dang blta bar mi nus la gang zhig reg pa dang blta bar nus pa'i chags yul gyi lus de ni khyod 'dod pa'i sems sam shes pa min na/_sha dang sems gang la brtags kyang chags pa'i don med bzhin du 'khyud cing zhen pa des ci zhig bya ste shin tu 'khrul bar zad do/_/
segments.translation_text: One may think, "I am not interested in those images; I wish to touch a body that has a mind.” But the mind that you desire has no form because it is not physical, and therefore it cannot be touched or looked at. The body of the object of attachment that you can see and touch is not the mind that you wish to encounter. Therefore, analyzing carefully, it is meaningless to desire either the fleshly body or the mind. What is the use of this desire to embrace? It is merely a delusion.

segments.translation_html:
It is not amazing that the nature of others’ bodies
Is not recognized as impure.
Yet it is amazing not to recognize
The impurity of one’s own body.

segments.translation_text: The body of the object of attachment is composed of many impure substances, but as this can only be inferred, it is not amazing that this isn’t realized. However, it is amazing not to realize that one’s own body is composed of many impurities, as these are directly experienced. This is extremely deluded.

[[Texts/Bodhicaryāvatāra/Verses/8.57|Verse 8.57]]  ·  [[Translation Memory:001-Tsadra-BCA-Root-Padmakara/577|Verse tm]]
segments.translation_html:
Having discarded a young lotus that has
Blossomed from the rays of a cloudless sun,
Why does this mind that clings to impurity
Find joy in a cage of impurity?

segments.translation_text: If one is attached to color, shape, smell, and touch, then it is appropriate to be attached to the freshness of a flower that blossoms and opens in cloudless sunlight. Ignoring that, with a mind that craves impurity, why enjoy a body which is just a basket or container filled with many impurities? Such attachment and enjoyment is inappropriate.

segments.translation_html:

segments.translation_html:

Why embrace another on your lap?

segments.translation_text: If one thinks, "I have no desire to touch or attachment to impurities such as feces and urine,” then Lustful One, why do you lust after and embrace upon your lap the body of the object of your attachment, which arises from the womb, which is like a field with many impurities, and which is developed by other impurities such as blood and semen. Therefore, it is unsuitable to be attached to others’ bodies that contaminate things.

segments.translation_html:
If you doubt, even though
Impurity is directly demonstrated thus,
Look at impure things
Such as corpses in cemeteries.

segments.translation_text: If one still wonders whether the body is by nature pure or impure, even with such direct evidence from the point of view of cause, result, and its own nature, then consider the body after it is thrown into the cemetery. segments.translation_text: If the body of the object of attachment is naked and not covered by clothes; not cleaned by shaving, bathing, and the like; the very long hair and nails are not trimmed; and the teeth not brushed, they become caked with stuff like rotten mud. The nature of that naked body would look as fearsome as a monster, or the lord of death. If that is the case, why put effort into bathing, washing, and anointing the body of the object of attachment? It is like sharpening and polishing a weapon that will injure one, and doing so is deluded.

segments.translation_text: Thus, the body of the object of attachment is impure and without essence, and also usually cannot be obtained without paying wealth as a price. As a result, this life is harmed by toil and weariness to acquire wealth for that purpose, and the next life will be harmed by the experience of severe suffering in hell as a result of non-virtuous deeds. Therefore, abandon conceptual thoughts of attachment to sentient beings.

segments.translation_html:

segments.translation_text: During childhood, due to inability to produce wealth, there can be no experience of pleasure based on wealth. During adulthood, due to the hardship of accumulating and guarding wealth, there can be no experience of pleasure based on wealth. If wealth is accumulated during adulthood, during old age when life is exhausted and ends, how can pleasure based on wealth be experienced, as there is no time or ability to use it?

segments.translation_html:
Some base, lustful ones,
Exhausted from working all day.
Return home with weary body,
And sleep like corpses.

segments.wylie: dod yon la chags pa dang ldan pa'i ngan pa kha cig ni nyin par rangs po zhing rmo ba dang*/_rtswa thu ba dang shing len pa la sogs pa'i las khur gyis yongs su dub cing ngal bar byas te/_nyi ma nub pa dang khyim du 'ongs nas thang chad pa'i lus mtshan mo rangs po shi ba'i ro dang 'dra bar nyal zhing gnyid log par byed la/_yang sad ma thag las dman pa de la 'jug pas khor yug tu sdug bsngal bar gnas so/_/
segments.translation_text: Some ordinary people, who have a strong attachment to material wealth, spend the whole day cultivating fields and doing agricultural work such as planting grass, or cutting wood. Through these and other mundane tasks they become completely exhausted and weary during the day. When the sun sets, they return home and their exhausted bodies sleep all night like corpses. Soon after awakening, they again engage in mundane activities. Day after day and night after night they experience this suffering.

segments.translation_text: Some work for others, although they wish to work for themselves. They are confused about how to obtain their own benefit, and sell their bodies for a period of time in order to gain some amount of money. Without gaining the happiness of the money they desire, they must perform many tasks for others and are blown about by the winds of their employers. Thus they experience suffering.

segments.translation_text: In the beginning, if wealth is lacking, it must be searched for, which is the suffering of accumulation. In the middle, there is the fear of the wealth being wasted or lost, which is the suffering of guarding it. In the end, the wealth will be taken by thieves or others, which is the suffering of losing it. Thus wealth is continuous suffering and produces constant anxiety in the beginning, middle, and end. Realize it as the root that produces suffering. Those whose minds are completely distracted by attachment to wealth have no time for meditation and therefore no opportunity become free of the suffering of samsara and to attain liberation. segments.translation_html:
What is desired will certainly disintegrate,
Causing falling into hell, etc.,
Despite constant hardship and weariness,
Not even for a great purpose.

segments.translation_text: The pleasures that arise from desire objects are unreliable and impermanent. Their nature is deceptive, and they suddenly disintegrate. Indulging in sin for their purpose will cause falling into the lower realms such as hell. Compared to the inexhaustible happiness of Buddhahood, the happiness obtained from desire objects is not great.

segments.translation_text: If even a millionth part of that hardship had been expended in the noble activities of the Enlightened Ones, Buddhahood itself could have been achieved. Although that is the case, those who are overcome with desire put aside the easiest, most beneficial, and appropriate method which is performing the conduct of the Bodhisattva, in preference for difficult, unsuitable methods. At the time of the cause, such methods entail great suffering, and at the time of the result, there is no happiness as in the enlightened state. Therefore, engaging in austerity for mundane purposes is extremely deluded.

Thinking from the point of view of cause, there are the faults of the object of desire, which is the base from which a variety of non-virtues arises. These cannot be compared even to being cut by weapons, killed by poison, burned by fire, vanquished by enemies, or falling from cliffs because the worst thing that will happen is the separation of body and mind; none of them can force lower rebirth. segments.translation_text: As explained above, disillusionment with the consequences of desire produces renunciation thought and also develops appreciation for and delight in the good qualities of isolation. There is no one with whom to compete, so arguments are avoided, and there are no objects of attachment and hatred, so defilement is avoided. Conceptual thoughts and violence are naturally pacified. Therefore dwell in peaceful groves and other enticing places.

segments.translation_text: But even greater than that are Bodhisattvas who have the fortune of the holy Dharma. They dwell upon a spacious, soft flat stone in the enticing chamber of a cave, cooled by moonlight which is far better than the sandalwood. In that pleasant and peaceful grove, there are no unpleasant words, and the happy feeling of gentle breezes is much better than the waving of fans. They walk about thinking only of how to benefit all sentient beings. This is far more exalted than the other, because it is effortless and free of attachment.
segments.translation_html: But even greater than that are Bodhisattvas who have the fortune of the holy Dharma. They dwell upon a spacious, soft flat stone in the enticing chamber of a cave, cooled by moonlight which is far better than the sandalwood. In that pleasant and peaceful grove, there are no unpleasant words, and the happy feeling of gentle breezes is much better than the waving of fans. They walk about thinking only of how to benefit all sentient beings. This is far more exalted than the other, because it is effortless and free of attachment.

segments.translation_text: One may dwell as long as desired in an empty house owned by no one, under a tree in an enticing forest, a deep cave or other place. There, all sufferings of clinging to the objects of desire and material things are abandoned as well as the need to guard them from harm. Feelings of hope, fear, and dependence on others are unnecessary as one dwells freely and flexibly without relying on others.

segments.translation_html:
Although the body has many parts such as the hands and the like,
Yet, as a whole they are protected as one;
Likewise, these many sentient beings with various sufferings and pleasures,
Are one in wishing to experience happiness, just like myself.

segments.wylie: dper na lag pa dang rkang pa dang mgo bo la sogs pa'i dbye bas phye na rnam pa mang po [p.-267] [[rab gsal snang ba]] yod na yang thams cad kyang bdag nyid kyis yongs su bsrung bar bya ba'i lus su gcig pa ltar don de bzhin du 'gro ba mtha' yas pa'i rigs drug so so'i sdug bsngal tha dad pa du ma yod kyang sems can thams cad kyang bdag nyid ji lta ba bzhin du sdug bsngal mi 'dod cing bde ba 'dod pa'i nyams can du gcig pa'i phyir bdag gzhan mnyam pa nyid du bsrung zhing bsgom par rigs so/_/
segments.translation_text: Just as the body can be classified into many different parts such as hands, legs, head, etc., yet all of the limbs are parts of the body and all need to be guarded and protected as a single unit, in the same way, the infinite sentient beings in the six realms all have various forms of suffering, yet just like oneself, all of these sentient beings are equal in that they do not wish to experience suffering, and they wish to experience happiness. Thus they are all the same. For that reason, it is suitable to meditate on equality of self and other and to protect them.

segments.translation_html: Just as the body can be classified into many different parts such as hands, legs, head, etc., yet all of the limbs are parts of the body and all need to be guarded and protected as a single unit, in the same way, the infinite sentient beings in the six realms all have various forms of suffering, yet just like oneself, all of these sentient beings are equal in that they do not wish to experience suffering, and they wish to experience happiness. Thus they are all the same. For that reason, it is suitable to meditate on equality of self and other and to protect them.

segments.translation_text: One might think, "It is not reasonable for the leg that hurts to be protected by the hand, but the physical body is a combination of various limbs that has long been thought to be a single body by the mind, therefore it is protected.” Anything that is unsuitable or causes suffering for oneself or others should be eliminated as much as possible, because the wish to protect arises due to long familiarization. From another point of view, abandon the thought of clinging to the body as a unitary self because it is unsuitable. Anything that is unsuitable to oneself or others should be discarded to the extent possible.

segments.translation_text: Some may think, "Others’ mental continua and assemblage of physical aggregates are not the same as my own, therefore, I will not protect them. But my own earlier and later life and mental continuum are the same, so I will protect myself now from my own future suffering. Throughout my life, my assembly of physical aggregates is the same, so it is suitable for my hand to protect my leg from pain.” This so-called continuum is actually the arising of multiple mental moments in succession. The so-called assemblage is a gathering of multiple limbs such as hands and legs, and these are mere labels, like ants traveling in a continuous line without break, which is called a garland of ants, like the gathering of an assembly of elephants, horses and people called an army. These are false; there is no true single entity, because they are multiple entities.

segments.translation_text: Ultimately, as no single self exists to experience the suffering, there is no difference at all between oneself and others. Relatively, all the sufferings of self and others are equal in the sense that they are suffering. Therefore, exert oneself to dispel these sufferings. What is the use of the firm conviction, "I will dispel my own but not others’ sufferings?” There is no benefit whatsoever. Therefore it is right to meditate on the enlightenment thought of equality of self and other.

segments.translation_text: They may argue, "If there is no self that is the experiencer of suffering, what is the reason to work to prevent the suffering of other beings?” This is a baseless argument. Although ultimately there is no self, on the relative level, everyone, even the Carvakas, works to dispel suffering and does not wish to experience it. Thus those who wish to dispel their own suffering because they do not wish to experience it, must also dispel the suffering of other sentient beings because the suffering is similar. Those who do not wish to dispel others’ suffering should not work to dispel their own suffering, as it is similar. Again, all of these sufferings should be dispelled.

segments.translation_html:

segments.translation_text: To describe this in more detail, once upon a time, there was a Buddha named Precious Guru Immaculate Moon Exalted King. When that Buddha’s doctrine had nearly diminished, there was a king named Shri Datta who dwelt in a palace known as Container of Jewels. Caught up in misconception, he exiled Bodhisattva Beautiful Moon Flower and others to a forest known as Noble in Every Aspect. Even realizing that his life was in danger, the great Bodhisattva returned to the king’s palace to teach the Dharma, as a result of which hundreds, thousands, and millions of sentient beings were placed in the irreversible state. Then the king ordered his executioner known as Producer of Joy, to gradually cut off the Bodhisattva’s legs and hands, and to extract both of his eyes, which killed him. When the Bodhisattva died, from his body, an amazing number of auspicious signs occurred. The king regretted his action, and supplicated the Bodhisattva. This was taught in the Samadhi Raja Sutra.

segments.translation_text: Since there is not even a tiny difference between oneself and others, just as one protects oneself from the slightest harm, such as a single unpleasant word, likewise, develop the compassionate thought that wishes to guard and protect other beings. Thus familiarize the mind that wishes to benefit others with the equality of self and other. Although this is difficult, through long practice it becomes possible.

segments.translation_text: Further, previously one clung to the thought, "I have good qualities,” and felt attachment to them, and clung to the thought, "Others possess faults,” and felt hatred to them. As an antidote to these and other faults, realize that one possesses others’ faults, and others possess oceans of one’s own good qualities. Therefore, completely relinquish holding oneself as exalted, and adopt thoughts that hold others as oneself, and perform the welfare of other beings. Thus strongly meditate.

segments.translation_text: One may wonder, "How could I exchange my single self for a multitude of sentient beings?” As an example, because of clinging to it as a body, this assembly of parts is believed to be one’s own single body, even though if split, there are many parts such as the hands and legs. Likewise, why can’t one believe that all of these limitless sentient beings are a part of oneself, or a branch of it? One must believe it. Thus it is possible to exchange oneself with multiple beings. Gradually through familiarization, this could arise.

Other beings are the self not arise?

segments.translation_text: For example, although there is no truly existing self, through familiarization from beginningless time, the thought that this physical body is my body has arisen. Likewise, through gradual familiarization, why could not the thought that the bodies of other sentient beings are my own also arise? By all means it could.

segments.translation_text: If clinging to self is not abandoned, due to clinging and attachment to one’s own body, fear arises from even the smallest of causes, like seeing one’s shadow as a ghost. Then what need to mention the source of great fears? Who among the intelligent would not see this body as an enemy? It is the source of the arising of a variety of fears. It is right to relinquish it with revulsion and not suitable to guard it with attachment.

segments.translation_html:
By wishing to keep the body alive,
And assuage hunger, thirst, and illness,
Birds, fish, and other animals
Are ambushed and killed.

segments.translation_text: If cherishing of oneself is not abandoned due to the wish to maintain one’s body, or to cure its diseases, or to protect it from hunger, thirst, cold, etc., or to find necessities such as food, drink, clothing, medicine, etc., some kill animals such as birds, fish, wild animals, and cattle. Others, like thieves or bandits, wait in ambush in order to steal or harm.

segments.translation_text: Such foolish ones in order to gain profit, service, and veneration think, "If this person lives, they will venerate me.” Thus they even murder their own parents who are noble objects, and even steal offerings to the Buddha and the Triple Gem, through which they accumulate negative karma. As a result, in the next life, they fall into the lower realms, such as Avici Hell, etc., and are burned by the terrible fires of suffering.

segments.translation_html:
Would the wise be attached to,
Venerate, or guard this body?
Who would not condemn this body
And regard it as an enemy?

segments.wylie: mkhas pa rnam dpyod dang ldan pa su zhig sdug bsngal thams cad kyi 'byung gnas su gyur pa'i lus de la dga' bas 'dod par byed cing brtse bas srung zhing skyong ba dang rnyed pas mchod par byed de byed pa ni mi rigs kyi nyes pa thams cad kyi rtsa ba lus 'di la mkhas pa su zhig dgra bo bzhin du blta bar mi byed cing brnyas par mi byed de dgra bzhin du blta zhing brnyas pa'i sgo nas ltos med du gzhan la gtang par rigs so/_/
segments.translation_text: Therefore, what wise person who is capable of intellectual analysis would joyfully love this body which is the source of the arising of every type of suffering? It is not suitable to lovingly guard, protect, and venerate it. Who among the wise would not regard it as an enemy that is the root of all faults? Who would not disparage it? It is right to disparage it, regard it as an enemy, and unconditionally give it to others.

segments.translation_html:
Thinking of one's own welfare, and saying
"What can I use if I give this? ” is the custom of ghosts.
Thinking of others' welfare, and saying
"What can I give if I use this? ” is the Dharma of the gods.

segments.wylie: gal te yo byad rnams gzhan la phyin na bdag ci zhig la longs spyad par bya zhes gzhan la mi ltos par bdag nyid gcig pu'i bde ba'i don sems pa ni 'dre yi tshul te ser sna'i dbang gis yi dwags dang sha za la sogs par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/_/gal te yo byad bdag gis longs spyad na gzhan la ci zhig sbyin par bya zhes rang don la mi ltos par gzhan mang po'i bde ba'i don sems pa ni lha yi chos te sbyin pa'i dbang gis tshangs pa dang brgya byin la sogs par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/_/
segments.translation_text: "If I give these things to others, what can I use for myself?” Thus thinking only of oneself, without regard for others is the manner of ghosts because, due to miserliness, one becomes a hungry ghost, flesh-eating ghost, etc. "If I use all of these things, what will I have to give to others?” Thus thinking of and wishing to benefit many others and disregarding one’s own purpose is the Dharma of the deities because, due to the power of giving, one becomes Brahma or Indra, etc.

segments.translation_html:
One who harms others for one's own sake,
Will be tormented in hell and the like.
One who harms themself for others’ sake,
Will attain every form of success.

segments.wylie: bdag gi bde ba bsgrub pa'i phyir du sems can gzhan gyi lus dang longs spyod la gnod pa byas na dmyal ba la sogs par [p.-277] [[rab gsal snang ba]] gdung ba drag po myong bar 'gyur zhing*/_gzhan la phan pa bsgrub pa'i phyir du bdag gi lus dang longs spyod la gnod pa byas na gnas skabs dang mthar thug gi phun sum tshogs pa thams cad thob par 'gyur ro/_/
segments.translation_text: If others’ bodies are harmed, or their wealth is reduced for the purpose of gaining happiness for oneself, one will experience severe suffering, such as hell, etc. However, if one’s own body or wealth is harmed in order to benefit others, all temporary and ultimate successes will be attained.

segments.translation_html: If others’ bodies are harmed, or their wealth is reduced for the purpose of gaining happiness for oneself, one will experience severe suffering, such as hell, etc. However, if one’s own body or wealth is harmed in order to benefit others, all temporary and ultimate successes will be attained.

segments.translation_html:
One who wishes to elevate themself,
Will become stupid and go to an evil lower birth,
One who transfers that to others.
Will be venerated and served in a higher birth.

segments.translation_text: One who wishes to attain higher status, such as a superior body, higher class or race, more retinue, or wealth, will fall in the next life into a lower status such as a lower birth, class or race, or less intelligence. By transferring whatever one desires to others, wishing them to attain higher status, all successes such as higher rebirth, veneration, and service will be attained.

segments.translation_html:
One who exploits others for the sake of themself,
Will experience slavery and the like.
One who uses themself for the sake of others,
Will experience lordliness and the like.

segments.translation_text: What need to elaborate? In short, ordinary childlike beings perform only their own benefit and do not even accomplish that; they experience only suffering in samsara. The Sages, who possess great compassion, perform only others’ benefit. Thus successfully accomplishing the two benefits; they experience great happiness. Look at the difference between these two and exert oneself in the exchange of self and others.

Thus in this life, masters will not receive service and veneration, and servants will not obtain even simple food and clothing.

segments.translation_html:
If successful pleasure and joy which accomplish
Both visible and invisible happiness are completely disregarded,
As a result of causing suffering for others,
The ignorant accept unbearable suffering.

segments.wylie: mthong ba'i chos tshe 'di dang ma mthong ba skye ba gzhan la bde ba rnam par dag pa 'grub pa'i phun sum tshogs pa'i bde ba dang skyid pa'i rgyu bdag gzhan brje ba yongs su bor zhing phan tshun mi 'dod pa sna tshogs bsgrubs te sdug bsngal 'ba' zhig byas pa'i rgyus blang dor gyi tshul la rmongs pa rnams dmyal ba la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal mi bzad pa dang du len pa ni shin tu snying rje ba'i gnas so/_/
segments.translation_text: Completely disregarding the exchange of self and other, which is a cause of magnificent joy and happiness that brings genuine happiness in this life which can be seen, and in the next life which cannot be seen, a multitude of undesirable things are acquired for oneself and others, and only suffering is experienced. Due to this, those who are deluded about what needs to be discarded and adopted voluntarily take on unbearable suffering, such as falling into hell, etc., and are therefore the objects of great compassion.

segments.translation_html:
If whatever violence exists in any world,
Whatever suffering and terrors exist,
All arise from clinging to the self,
What use is this great ghost to me?

segments.wylie: khor ba ma stongs kyi bar du 'jig rten dag na gzhan gyi gnod pa la sogs pa'i 'tshe ba gang yod pa dang*/_dgra dang dug sbrul la sogs pa'i 'jigs pa thams cad dang skye rga na 'chi la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal gang ji snyed yod par gyur pa de dag kun rtsa ba bdag tu 'dzin pa las byung bar gyur pa yin na/_'dre chen po dang 'dra bar gnod pa 'ba' zhig byed pa'i bdag 'dzin des ko bdag la ci zhig bya ste ci'ang dgos pa med do/_/
segments.translation_text: In every world until the end of samsara, all violence such as being harmed by others; all fears such as enemies and poison snakes; all sufferings such as birth, old age, illness, and death, etc., are all rooted in clinging to the self. Therefore, the self is like a great ghost that causes only harm. What use is this self-clinging? It is of no benefit or use whatsoever.

segments.translation_text: Before engaging in the practice of exchanging self and other, feelings of jealousy, competition, and pride arose toward those perceived to be higher than, equal to, and lower than oneself respectively. Having exchanged self and other, imagine those sentient beings as Bodhisattvas, and now name them "the new self.” Become familiar with those who are lower than, equal to, or higher than oneself as the embodiment of Bodhisattvas. Then oneself is named "the old self.”

segments.translation_text: From this point onward, understand that the words "that one” refer to the old self with which one has been familiar since beginningless time. The word "I” refers to other sentient beings who are newly adopted as the self. In brief, one has taken the role of other beings, and other beings have taken one’s own role. With this perception, be diligent in the practice of exchanging self and others. In this world, also, there are some traditions in which one must imagine oneself as another, and it is said that such thoughts arise in these people. Here, what is known as jealousy, competition and pride, which are things to be abandoned, are in reality an antidote to self cherishing.

segments.translation_text: Thus, if sentient beings are thought to be inferior due to moral lapses, wrong views, and inferior livelihoods, they are under the power of another, such as the defilements. I the sentient being did not do these things intentionally. Therefore, it is not right to look down on me in this respect. If that old self had the good quality of compassion, etc., he should help me the sentient being however he can, by curing the disease of my defilements. If there is some way to cure them, then I would even voluntarily suffer hardship.

དེ་ལྟ་ནའང་སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་འཆལ་བ་དང༌། ལྟ་བ་ངན་པ་དང༌། འཚོ་བ་རྒུད་པ་ལ་སོགས་པས་དམན་པའོ་སྙམ་ན། དེ་དག་ནི༵་ཉོན་མོངས་པའི་གཞན་དབང་དུ་གྱུར་པའི་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་བྱུང་བ་ཡིན་གྱི། སེམས་ཅན་བདག་ལ་རང་དབང་ཡོད་བཞིན་དུ་[p.-282][[རབ་གསལ་སྣང་བ་]]

segments.translation_text: Also, those sentient beings who performed sinful actions and fell into lower births and lower realms dwell as if they were between the jaws of a cruel animal. Not only does that old self lack the compassionate thought to benefit them by freeing them from suffering, but that old self possesses conceit and pride. He thinks he has exalted qualities, although he has none, and he wishes to challenge the learned and defeat them. This is not a proper attitude. Thus meditate jealousy.

segments.translation_text: Now, the old self has defilements and is inferior to me, the sentient being. segments.translation_html:
Renounce all pleasures;
Apply others’ suffering to myself.
By thinking, "How am I doing?”
Analyze my own faults.

segments.translation_text: As for me, I must free myself from attachment to experiences of pleasure and enjoyment, and voluntarily accept other beings’ suffering and apply it to myself. segments.translation_text: Thus abide single pointedly in the virtues explained above, such as activities suitable for performing others’ benefit. O Mind, do not engage in unsuitable actions, such as performing your own benefit. Thus all actions of the body, voice, and mind should be well-controlled, like a well-tamed horse, and engage only in suitable actions. If you fall from or transgress this and come under the domination of defilements, make efforts to destroy them by the power of the antidote.

segments.translation_html: Thus abide single pointedly in the virtues explained above, such as activities suitable for performing others’ benefit. O Mind, do not engage in unsuitable actions, such as performing your own benefit. Thus all actions of the body, voice, and mind should be well-controlled, like a well-tamed horse, and engage only in suitable actions. If you fall from or transgress this and come under the domination of defilements, make efforts to destroy them by the power of the antidote.

To that degree, I will fall into
A state of intolerance.

segments.translation_text: Thus, this body becomes feeble through attachment. The characteristic of its desire cannot be fulfilled even with wealth that covers the entire earth, so then who could fulfill the desires of this excessively lustful one? This is like King Ngalenu who became the owner of four continents, and even gained half of the throne of Indra, king of the gods, but as he was still not satisfied, fell to earth again.

segments.translation_text: Any noble being who does not expect to acquire desire objects for their own sake, and does not depend upon them will constantly acquire inexhaustible magnificent wealth. Therefore, I shall never open up an opportunity to become attached to even the most basic wealth for the purpose of increasing the body’s pleasure. Not grasping at attractive things is the most exalted among all fine possessions.

segments.translation_html:
Exhausted into ashes in the end,
Immovable, yet moved by others,
This unbearable, impure form,
Why hold it as a self?

segments.wylie: lus 'di bsrungs shing bskyangs kyang tha mar shi ba na mes bsregs nas thal ba'i mthar gtugs par 'gyur shing*/_da lta gson pa na yang rang gi ngo bo rdo ba ltar mi g.yo zhing gzhan yid dang rlung gi bskyod par bya dgos pa mi gtsang ba sna tshogs las grub pa'i gzugs ni mi bzad cing 'jigs su rung ba la 'di la ci'i phyir bdag tu 'dzin te de ltar 'dzin cing zhen pa ni 'khrul ba'o/_/
segments.translation_text: Although this body is protected and guarded, in the end when it dies, it will be cremated and become ashes and dirt. At this moment it is perceived as alive, but still its real nature is unmoving like stone. It must be moved by something else, such as the mind and airs. The body is composed of various impure substances, and has an unbearably fearsome appearance, so why cling to it as the self? Thus clinging and attachment to it are delusions.

segments.translation_text: Whether you are alive or will soon be dead, O Mind, what benefit is this body which is nothing but a magical machine made of impure substances? If you do not train your body and apply it to the holy Dharma, what is the difference between your body, and other material things like a piece of charcoal, or horse dung? If there is no difference, O Mind, why not give up the proud thought, "This is my body?” Thus, abandonment and revulsion are appropriate.

segments.translation_text: Also, while alive, I protect and benefit this body with food and clothing, yet at the end, when it will die and be eaten by jackals and vultures and dismantled, if I will have no hatred toward those who will mercilessly eat the material body that was cherished and protected, then why be attached to a thing that does not understand whether it was done or not? It is not suitable to have attachment and clinging to it.

segments.translation_text: It is not right to cling to this body for the purpose of one’s own welfare. Therefore, O Mind, protect this body without any attachment or conditions at all, in order to provide vast benefit to all sentient beings. Because it is needed for others’ benefit, even though the body has a multitude of faults such as being filled with impure things, still it is necessary to keep and protect it like workers keep a tool they need to use.

segments.translation_text: In order to abandon defilements, the mind must rest in meditative absorption. Since the ordinary meaningless behavior of worldly childlike beings has already been experienced countless times before, this is enough. From now onward, I will follow the footsteps of many noble wise beings, such as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Just as a commitment was made to follow their precepts and to remember what was explained about heedful behavior of body, voice, and mind in the fourth chapter and in the Compendium of Precepts, I will exert myself in repelling and abandoning sleep, sluggishness, scattering, regret, and the like which contradict meditative absorption.

segments.translation_text: Develop courage and stable patience for all activities that are right and suitable to be performed, according to the holy biographies of Sons of Jinas that one has seen. This completes the explanation of the eighth chapter of Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas, the principal topic of which is how to dwell in meditative absorption.[p.324][[A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas]]
Gyaltsen, Lama Kalsang, and Ani Kunga Chodron, trans. ''A Commentary on Shantideva's Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas Written by Sazang Mati Panchen: Known as An Extremely Clear Illumination of the Meaning of the Text''. Walden, NY: Tsechen Kunchab Ling, 2019. First edition published by The Yeshe Dorje Foundation in 2006.
